announcements.text: Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Minneapolis, Minnesota, was awarded an $862,848,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to manufacture, inspect, test, package and deliver M1156 precision guidance kits and variants. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 3, 2031. Army Contracting Command, Newark, New Jersey, is the contracting activity (W15QKN-26-D-A072).

Research Innovations Inc.,* Alexandria, Virginia, was awarded a $99,529,577 firm-fixed-price indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for procurement, delivery and sustainment of Dragonfly systems. Bids were solicited via the internet with 95 received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 2, 2031. Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W56KGY-26-D-A002).

Abt Global LLC, Rockville, Maryland (W912HQ-26-D-A008); Booz Allen Hamilton Inc., McLean, Virginia (W912HQ-26-D-A009); CDM Federal Programs Corp., Fairfax, Virginia (W912HQ-26-D-A010); Stantec Consulting Services Inc., Denver, Colorado (W912HQ-26-D-A011); OM Group Inc.,* Piscataway, New Jersey (W912HQ-26-D-A012); and Taylor-Woolpert LLC,* Jacksonville, Florida (W912HQ-26-D-A013), will compete for each order of the $49,902,262 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for navigation and civil works data analysis and system support professional services. Bids were solicited via the internet with 13 received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 3, 2026. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Humphreys Engineer Center Support Activity, Fort Belvoir, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

Grose Construction LLC,* Aberdeen, Maryland, was awarded a $24,500,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for construction services supporting small construction, repair and modernization projects for depot buildings and facilities. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 14, 2031. Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal, Michigan, is the contracting activity (W912GY-26-D-A001).

Artisan Consulting Engineers LLC,* Chapin, Illinois (N62473-26-D-0025), TABCON Inc.,* Queen Creek, Arizona (N62473-26-D-0027); J. Davis Construction Management Inc.,* Oxnard, California (N62473-26-D-0028); Southwest Construction & Property Management,* San Bruno, California (N62473-26-D-0029); and Souza Construction,* Farmersville, California (N62473-26-D-0030), are awarded a combined $200,000,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity multiple award contract. This contract provides for new construction, renovation, and repair of roofing projects. Work will be performed at various installations located in California (95%), Arizona (1%), Nevada (1%), Utah (1%), Colorado (1%), and New Mexico (1%), and is expected to complete by September 2034. The maximum dollar value, including the two-year base period and six option periods of one year, for all five contracts is $200,000,000. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $5,000 for each awardee will be obligated at the time of award to satisfy the minimum guarantee and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with 16 offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southwest, San Diego, California is the contracting activity.

General Dynamics Missions Systems Inc., Pittsfield, Massachusetts, is being awarded a $194,139,485 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (PZ0002) to a previously awarded unpriced letter contract (N0003026C7000). This value includes optional line items. The effort will provide technical and engineering support for the Fire Control Subsystem in support of the Nuclear-Armed, Sea-Launched Cruise Missile Program. Work will be performed in Pittsfield, Massachusetts (75%); and Manassas, Virginia (25%). Work is expected to be completed on Sept. 30, 2028. Fiscal 2025 reconciliation research, development, test and evaluation, Navy funding in the amount of $135,303,302 will be obligated on this award. No funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was awarded as a sole source acquisition pursuant to 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and was previously synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) online portal. Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Integrated Solutions for Systems Inc., * Huntsville, Alabama, is awarded a $47,768,691 Firm Fixed Price contract for expeditionary maintenance and repair facility (EMRF) production. The program is for the fabrication of five fully outfitted EMRFs, consisting of 90 individual expeditionary maintenance and repair container (EMRC) prototype units and four additional fully outfitted EMRC variants. The EMRF with additional EMRC variants will be deployed globally to diverse environments where the government will use them as data collection platforms to validate the EMRF concept. Work will be performed in Huntsville, Alabama, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) $47,768,691 funding will be obligated at award and not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract is a sole-source Small Business Innovation Research Phase III award, under 15 U.S. Code 638 (r)(4). The Mid Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity (N5005426C0002).

Dynetics Inc., Huntsville, Alabama, was awarded a $40,776,966 hybrid other transaction agreement modification to manufacture, deliver and support 14 medium range air defense radar (MRADR) production representative model systems. The hybrid modification also requires depot level technical manual support, program management support, engineering change proposals, associated program management, logistics support, software support, and retrofit four MRADR prototype systems and four Marine Expeditionary Long Range Persistent Sensor systems. Work will be performed at Huntsville, Alabama (87.5%); and Woodlake, California (12.5%), and is expected to be completed in August 2028. The maximum dollar value is $40,776,966. Fiscal 2025 procurement (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $2,972,730; fiscal 2026 Procurement (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $31,295,685; and fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $1,500,000, are obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The requirement was procured under the authority of 10 U.S. Code 4022 as a follow-on agreement to the prototype agreement (M67854-23-9-0023). Marine Corps Systems Command, Quantico, Virginia, is the contracting activity (M67854-25-9-0122).

The Boeing Co., Seattle, Washington, is awarded a $31,505,637 modification (P00002) to a cost-plus-fixed-fee order (N0001925F0254) against previously issued basic ordering agreement (N0001921G0006). This modification exercises options for P-8A platform sustainment support, support equipment maintenance, engineering investigations, and integrated maintenance augmentation support for the Navy and the governments of Australia, the United Kingdom, Norway, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, and Germany. Work will be performed in Jacksonville, Florida (25%); Whidbey Island, Washington (15%); Sigonella, Italy (6%); Manama, Bahrain (6%); Kaneohe Bay, Hawaii (5%); Patuxent River, Maryland (5%); Keflavik, Iceland (5%); Kadena, Japan (5%); Misawa, Japan (5%); Seattle, Washington (2.5%); Oceana, Virginia (2.5%); Fayetteville, Tennessee (2.5%); Mesa, Arizona (2.5%); Dayton, Ohio (2.5%); Columbus, Ohio (2.5%); Fort Walton Beach, Florida (2.5%); Huntsville, Alabama (2.5%); various locations within the continental U.S. (1%); and various locations outside the continental U.S. (2%), and is expected to be completed in September 2027. Fiscal 2024 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $8,576,380; fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $8,922,792; Foreign Military Sales customer funds in the amount of $2,745,842; and Royal Australian Air Force cooperative funds in the amount of $277,003 will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was not competed. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

ATAP Inc.,* Eastaboga, Alabama (N00174-26-D-1016); Brooks & Perkins Inc.,* Cadillac, Michigan (N00174-26-D-1017); Central Metal Fabricators Inc.,* Farmingdale, New Jersey (N00174-26-D-1018); Cardinal Scientific Inc.,* Waldorf, Maryland (N00174-26-D-1019); Greene Machine & Manufacturing Co.,* Macon, Georgia (N00174-26-D-1020); BK Manufacturing Co., doing business as BK Aerospace,* Arab, Alabama (N00174-26-D-1021); and Bent River Machine,* Clarkdale, Arizona (N00174-26-D-1022), are awarded a combined $31,000,000 firm-fixed-price, multiple award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts for the manufacture, assembly, testing, and spare parts of ordnance handling equipment. Each awardee will be awarded $500 (minimum contract guarantee per awardee) at time of award. Work will be performed in Eastaboga, Alabama; Clarkdale, Arizona; Arab, Alabama; Cadillac, Michigan; Waldorf, Maryland; Farmingdale, New Jersey; and Macon, Georgia and is expected to be completed by August 2031. Fiscal 2026 weapons procurement, Navy appropriated funds in the amount of $3,500 will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. All other funding will be made available at the delivery order level as contracting actions occur. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website with seven offers received. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division, Indian Head, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0017426D1016 through N0017426D1022).

Appleton Marine Inc,* Appleton, Wisconsin, is awarded a $23,790,647 hybrid cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity supply contract with incidental services for the fabrication, testing, and shipping of new Slewing Arm Davits built in accordance with Navy specified drawings, which are used on various classes of Naval Ships. It is estimated that work will be performed at the Contractor’s facility in Appleton, Wisconsin (77.35%), and various government locations (22.65%). Government locations include the following: Norfolk, Virginia (4.53%); San Diego, California (4.53%); Mayport, Florida (4.53%); Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (4.53%); and Bremerton, Washington (4.53%). Performance is expected to be completed by September 2031. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funding in the total amount of $1,697,392 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. All other funding will be made available at the task order level as contracting actions occur. This contract was competitively procured via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment website with two offers received. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N64498-26-D-1032).

Lockheed Martin Corp. Rotary and Mission Systems, Moorestown, New Jersey, is awarded a $17,788,458 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to previously awarded contract N6339425C0005 to exercise options for Aegis design agent field engineering services. Work will be performed in San Diego, California (27%); Yokosuka, Japan (23%); Mayport, Florida (14%); Seattle, Washington (11%); Norfolk, Virginia (10%); Rota, Spain (6%); Pearl Harbor, Hawaii (6%); and Port Hueneme, California (3%), and is expected to be completed by September 2027. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,116,252 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Surface Warfare Center Port Hueneme Division, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity.

Lockheed Martin Corp., Syracuse, New York, is awarded a $14,600,000 firm-fixed-price delivery order (N00024-26-F-6263) under a previously awarded indefinite-delivery/indefinite quantity contract (N00024-25-D-6211) for AN/BLQ-10 spares for submarine electronic warfare systems on new construction and in-service submarines. Work will be performed in Syracuse, New York, and is expected to be completed by February 2028. Fiscal 2025 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $14,292,045 (98%); and fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $307,955 (2%), will be obligated at the time of award, of which, $307,955 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems, Moorestown, New Jersey, is awarded a $9,453,398 cost-plus-incentive-fee and cost-only modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-15-C-5151) for Aegis Ship Integration and Test program support. Work will be performed in Moorestown, New Jersey, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,440,920 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

SSA Atlantic LLC, Savannah, Georgia (HTC711-26-D-E120), was awarded a $72,742,360 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to obtain stevedoring and related terminal services. Work will be performed at the Ports of Charleston, South Carolina; Savannah, Georgia; Wilmington, North Carolina; and Morehead City, North Carolina. Work is expected to be completed by Sept. 30, 2031. This contract was competitively procured with proposals solicited via the System for Award Management website, and one offer was received. Fiscal 2027 transportation working capital funds are being obligated at the time of award. The contract has a total cumulative face value of $90,927,949. U.S. Transportation Command, Directorate of Acquisition, Scott Air Force Base, Illinois, is the contracting activity.

Sierra Nevada Co. LLC, Englewood, Colorado, has been awarded a $30,967,151 cost-plus-fixed-fee and cost-reimbursement modification (P00037) to a previously awarded contract (FA2834-24-C-B002) for the Survivable Airborne Operations Center. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract from $13,082,081,647 to $13,113,048,798. Work will be performed at Englewood, Colorado, and is expected to be completed by Dec. 31, 2027. Fiscal 2025 research, development, testing and evaluation funds in the amount of $5,115,516; and fiscal 2026 research, development, testing and evaluation funds in the amount of $10,610,452, are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Hanscom Air Force Base, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity.
